caption: The drawing depicts a ceramic object resembling a bird, likely a duck or similar waterfowl, with distinct textural and decorative elements. The object is primarily brown with darker and lighter shades to highlight its three-dimensional form. The bird's body forms the main vessel, which sits on a slightly rounded base that appears integrated with the overall shape. The back of the bird has a textured, oval surface pattern, while the sides are decorated with several circular motifs. The neck is elongated and slightly curved, topped with a rounded head featuring detailed eyes, nostrils, and an open beak. A thick, arched handle is attached to the back near what would be the bird’s wings. On one side, near the handle and back, there is a cylindrical spout or protrusion. The overall background is a light, slightly yellowed paper, and the bird-shaped vessel is centrally positioned with no other objects present. There is a faint signature visible near the bottom right of the drawing.
title: Glazed Pottery Duck Bottle
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
